rule.description: A named parameter group of three or more items, identified by (name, type) pairs, that recurs through the parameter lists of four or more distinct function or method signatures in production (non-test) Go code is a data clump. Blank, unnamed and variadic parameters never join a group; receivers are not parameters; only maximal groups are reported.

checks.description: Detect signatures that re-declare the table's border framing (border definition, border style, left/right/column separator toggles, column widths) as separate parameters.
checks.detected_relation: signature -> recurring parameter group [border lipgloss.Border, borderStyle lipgloss.Style, borderLeft bool, borderRight bool, borderColumn bool, widths []int]
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The frame context is consumed jointly by every builder that draws part of the table frame; re-receiving it member-by-member in signature after signature means the framing is never captured by one abstraction.

matches.evidence: constructTopBorder(border lipgloss.Border, borderStyle lipgloss.Style, borderLeft, borderRight, borderColumn bool, widths []int): top border builder declares the full frame context.
constructBottomBorder(border lipgloss.Border, borderStyle lipgloss.Style, borderLeft, borderRight, borderColumn bool, widths []int): bottom border builder declares the same group again.

func (t *Table) constructHeaders(border lipgloss.Border, borderStyle lipgloss.Style, borderLeft, borderRight, borderHeader, borderColumn bool, headers []string, hasHeaders bool, widths, heights []int): header builder threads the frame context plus the grid data.

func (t *Table) constructRow(index int, isOverflow bool, border lipgloss.Border, borderStyle lipgloss.Style, borderRow, borderLeft, borderRight, borderColumn bool, headers []string, hasHeaders bool, wrap bool, widths, heights []int, overflowHeight int): row builder (used for data and overflow rows) re-declares the frame context among fourteen parameters.

checks.description: Detect signatures that re-declare the horizontal layout policy (left/right/column separator toggles plus the wrap switch) as separate parameters.
checks.detected_relation: signature -> recurring parameter group [borderLeft bool, borderRight bool, borderColumn bool, wrap bool]
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The layout policy crosses the table/resizing boundary and flows back into row construction; identifying it requires inspecting signatures in two files of the same package, and it is never carried as one named policy.

matches.evidence: func (r *resizer) optimizedWidths(borderLeft, borderRight, borderColumn, wrap bool): the sizing entry passes the layout policy down to both direction passes.
func (r *resizer) expandTableWidth(borderLeft, borderRight, borderColumn, wrap bool): the expand pass re-declares the same policy and forwards wrap to row-height expansion.
func (r *resizer) shrinkTableWidth(borderLeft, borderRight, borderColumn, wrap bool): the shrink passes (largest-first and median-based) re-declare the same policy again.

func (t *Table) constructRow(index int, isOverflow bool, border lipgloss.Border, borderStyle lipgloss.Style, borderRow, borderLeft, borderRight, borderColumn bool, headers []string, hasHeaders bool, wrap bool, widths, heights []int, overflowHeight int): the row builder receives the same policy the resizer passed among its own signatures, closing the loop across the two files.

checks.description: Detect signatures that re-declare the tree's enumeration context (children, the enumerator, and the enumerator style function) as separate parameters.
checks.detected_relation: signature -> recurring parameter group [children Children, enumerator Enumerator, enumeratorFunc StyleFunc]
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The enumeration context belongs to a subtree's rendering configuration; relaying children, enumerator and its style function independently through each prefix and child helper leaves the configuration without an owner.

matches.evidence: enumPrefix(children Children, i int, enumerator Enumerator, enumeratorFunc StyleFunc): single-prefix helper takes the enumeration context plus the index it actually needs.
maxEnumPrefix(children Children, enumerator Enumerator, enumeratorFunc StyleFunc): the sibling-alignment pass re-declares the context to measure every child prefix.

renderChildren(children Children, prefix string, enumerator Enumerator, indenter Indenter, rootStyle lipgloss.Style, enumeratorFunc, indenterFunc, itemFunc StyleFunc, width int, maxLen int): the children loop threads the enumeration context alongside the wider render configuration.

renderChild(children Children, i int, prefix string, enumerator Enumerator, indenter Indenter, rootStyle lipgloss.Style, enumeratorFunc, indenterFunc, itemFunc StyleFunc, width int, maxLen int): the per-child helper re-declares the enumeration context among eleven parameters and forwards parts of it onward.

excluded.reason: Threads an overlapping slice of the tree's render configuration (enumerator, indenter, root style, three style functions, width) but contains no complete recurring group: it has no children parameter, and nobody of its parameter combination recurs in four or more signatures, so the rule anchors on the helpers that hold a complete group.

Declare the three horizontal separator flags only; that group is a proper subset of the maximal layout-policy quartet (which adds wrap) and of the border-frame group, so the rule reports only the maximal groups and these signatures inherit the cost without being anchored.

Share the vertical separator quartet (borderTop, borderBottom, borderHeader, borderRow), but it recurs in only two signatures, below the rule's support threshold of four; extending it further would have required threading flags into consumers that use none of them.

excluded.location: table/table.go: Table.resize; tree/tree.go: Tree.String and the styling setters
excluded.reason: The assembly points that fan struct state out into the recurring arguments; they take no parameters themselves, so the rule, which evaluates parameter lists, credits their relays rather than these sources.
Test signatures never join a rule group; the rule analyzes production (non-test) Go code only.
